---
title: "Deployment Configuration: Personas and User Functionalities"
---

## What is a "persona"?

When SPARMVET is deployed, it is configured with a **deployment profile** — a named set of flags that control which functionalities are available to the end user. These profiles are called **personas**.

A persona is not a user account, a role, or a permission system. It is simply a named configuration loaded at startup that determines the user interface and available features for that deployment.

The term "persona" reflects a design intent: the same underlying system can present itself differently depending on its deployment context — as a read-only pipeline viewer, an interactive research tool, or a developer workbench.

---

## User functionalities

Rather than thinking about personas first, think about **what you want your users to be able to do**. SPARMVET offers the following user functionalities:

| Functionality | What the user can do |
|---|---|
| **View** | Browse visualisations and pre-processed results (T2 tier). Always available. |
| **Passive filter** | Temporarily explore data by filtering rows or hiding columns. Changes are ephemeral — nothing is recorded, resets on reload. |
| **Active filter / T3 audit** | Justify and commit data decisions (e.g. exclude outliers with a documented reason). Creates a permanent T3 branch, written to the audit trail. |
| **Export** | Download a reproducible bundle (plots, data, wrangling recipe, audit trail, provenance README). |
| **Import — metadata** | Upload a replacement metadata file (overwrites existing metadata; triggers data rebuild). |
| **Import — full data** | Map all raw data files to the manifest (includes metadata; overwrites existing data). |
| **Gallery** | Browse 34+ chart recipe templates with 6-axis taxonomy filtering. |
| **Blueprint Architect** | Inspect and design manifest lineage (TubeMap visualisation, manifest navigator). |
| **Test Lab** | Generate synthetic test data, bootstrap manifest templates, run reconciliation checks. |

---

## Non-negotiable dependencies

Some functionalities are tightly coupled — activating one without the others creates a broken or scientifically misleading experience. These are enforced as startup validation rules (a `PersonaConfigError` is raised if violated):

### T3 audit requires a full supporting stack

If T3 is activated, **all of the following must also be activated**:

- Comparison mode — so users can see T2 vs T3 side by side
- Audit report — so decisions are recorded
- Session management + autosave — so work-in-progress is not lost
- Export — so the justified decisions can be shared
- Both tier toggles (T1↔T2 and T2↔T3)

**Rationale:** T3 is a scientific decision-making tool. Activating it without the ability to record, compare, and export those decisions defeats its purpose. These capabilities are two sides of the same scientific workflow: *justify → record → export*.

### Full import implies metadata import

Activating full data import (`import_helper_enabled`) automatically implies metadata import is also available. There is no deployment configuration where full import is available but metadata import is not.

---

## What deployers can freely configure

The following are independent choices:

- Whether passive filter / tier toggle are shown
- Whether export is available
- Whether import is available, and at what level
- Whether Gallery, Blueprint, or Test Lab are accessible
- UI branding (project title, subtitle, persona badge)
- Whether the manifest selector is shown or locked to a specific manifest

---

## Audit trail — always on

Every export — regardless of persona configuration — always includes a complete provenance record:

- SHA256 of raw source data (`data_batch_hash`)
- SHA256 of the manifest (`manifest_sha256`)
- SHA256 of the wrangling recipe (`decision_hash`)
- Git commit hash and release version of the software
- Export creation timestamp
- Manifest name and path
- Active persona ID
- Active data tier (T1 / T2 / T3)
- Software versions (Python, plotnine, polars)
- Relative paths of all raw data files loaded
- T3 audit recipe (when T3 is active and has committed decisions)

This is not a flag. It cannot be disabled. It is a fundamental design commitment to scientific transparency and reproducibility.

For image exports (PNG, SVG, PDF), a subset of this provenance is additionally embedded in the **file metadata** (not visible in the image display) — so the provenance survives extraction from a bundle and travels with the file.

---

## Provided deployment configurations

SPARMVET ships with the following named configurations. These are starting points — deployers can create custom configurations by composing functionalities within the rules above.

| Profile name | Intended context | Key capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| `pipeline-static` | Read-only pipeline output display | View only, export bundle |
| `demo-vetinst` | Branded institutional demo | View only, no export, custom title |
| `web-demo` | Public web display | View only, custom branding |
| `pipeline-exploration-simple` | Pipeline users who explore data | Passive filter, tier toggle, export |
| `pipeline-exploration-advanced` | Pipeline users with audit capability | Full T3, comparison, session, export |
| `project-independent` | Research project — full capability | T3, import, gallery, blueprint, export |
| `developer` | Full development access | Everything including Test Lab |
| `qa` | Automated testing | All flags on (autosave off) |

### Proposed configurations (not yet implemented)

| Profile name | Intended context |
|---|---|
| `web-project-showcase` | Public website with branded static display |
| `lightweight-exploration` | Passive filter, minimal UI, export |

---

## Creating a custom configuration

1. Copy any existing template from `config/ui/templates/`
2. Set flags according to the user functionality matrix in `.antigravity/design/persona_capability_matrix.md`
3. Validate cascade rules (see `.antigravity/design/functionality_dependency_map.md`)
4. Set `SPARMVET_PERSONA=your-config-name` at launch

The startup validator will raise a `PersonaConfigError` if cascade rules are violated, with a descriptive message identifying which co-flags are missing.
